svg.aria-label: Two load models side by side. On the left, the common mistake: a thread firing requests back to back with no pauses against a single endpoint, sharing one connection. It answers the question of how fast the server can serve one endpoint. On the right, a virtual user: its own account and login, a loop across several endpoints, with real pauses between actions and a realistic read to write mix. It answers the question of how many people the server can serve. The caption says both numbers are real and only the second one is a capacity answer, and that quoting the first as a user count is the commonest way a load test misleads.
svg.text: A VIRTUAL USER IS NOT A THREAD
